c74object.name: evi.gigaverb~
c74object.digest: Classic gigaverb reverb algorithm, mono in / stereo out, fdn / allpass
c74object.description: A mono-in, stereo-out reverb implementation by Juhana Sadeharju. Originally Max/MSP-ified by Olaf Matthes (2004) Version 1.0test5, (c) 1999-2006 Juhana Sadeharju / Olaf Matthes. Originally Gen-ified by Graham Wakefield (2011). 64-bit MSP reference version by Volker Böhm (2016). This evieve version with updated filtering and parameter smooting. Attribute descriptions in this documentation are mainly from the Olaf Matthes originals.

inlet.digest: Audio In Mono or Left or 1 / messages to evi.gigaverb~
inlet.description: Mono, Left or 1 depends on the 'stereo' attribute.

inlet.digest: Audio In Nothing or Right or 2 / messages to evi.gigaverb~
inlet.description: Nothing, Right or 2 depends on the 'stereo' attribute.

method.name: anything
method.digest: In left inlet, messages to evi.gigaverb~
method.description: Prepending the word 'pattrstorage' allows you to send any message pattrstorage understands to the internal pattrstorage object - you can recieve pattrstorage output via the far right outlet.

attribute.name: bandwidth
attribute.description: 'This is like a damping control for the input, it has a similar effect to the damping control, but is subtly different.'

attribute.name: bypass
attribute.description: 'Bypass, signal unaffected when set to 1. Can be used to compare reverb signal with original signal and to save CPU power when gigaverb~ is not used.'

attribute.name: damping
attribute.digest: Normalised 0..1, lowpass if 1, bypass if 0, shelving in between
attribute.description: 'This controls the high frequency damping (a lowpass filter), values near 0 will make it sound very bright, values near 1 will make it sound very dark.'

attribute.name: early
attribute.description: 'The quantity of early reflections (scatter reflections directly from the source). Think of Lexicon's ambiance patches.'

attribute.name: highfrequency
attribute.description: High frequency point in Hz of the end of wet chain onepole shelving filters.

attribute.name: highgain
attribute.description: ± gain of the high shelving onpole filters. Negative values damp, positive values boost. -1..1 equates to approximately -10..10 dB.

attribute.name: late
attribute.description: 'The level of the classic reverb tail reflections.'

attribute.name: lowfrequency
attribute.description: Low frequency point in Hz of the end of wet chain onepole shelving filters.

attribute.name: lowgain
attribute.description: ± gain of the low shelving onpole filters. Negative values damp, positive values boost. -1..1 equates to approximately -10..10 dB.

attribute.name: reverb
attribute.description: 'Reverb decay time, in seconds. 7 is a good place to start. 0.1..360 seconds'

attribute.name: size
attribute.description: 'The size of the room, in meters. Excessively large, and excessively small values will make it sound a bit unrealistic. Values of around 30 sound good.'

attribute.name: smoothtime
attribute.description: Set the smoothing time in ms of all the internal parameter smoothing functions.

attribute.name: spread
attribute.description: Stereo spread (or 'width'), offsets L/R levels. Note, in Juhana Sadeharju and Graham Wakefield verions this is not available (fixed). In Olaf Matthes version this is object creation argument only. In evieve this can be modified in realtime at any time.

attribute.name: stereo
attribute.description: This is essentially a mono-in stereo-out reverb, but you can toggle 'stereo' 'on' ('1') to explicitly control L/R signals into the late diffusion section (and dry L/R). Default '0' 'off' (mono-in, stereo-out).

c74object.discussion: Note, in this evieve version there are slight differences in sound from the various Max versions, but this version is closer to the original (Sadeharju) and with slightly more diffuseness in the early taps and low-mid.
